Rashi on Gittin 71a:10:1.english: What, is it not [business] of others - which is testimony:

Rashi on Gittin 71a:11:1.english: They did not follow his signaling - to consider him as a competent person:

Rashi on Gittin 71a:11:2.hebrew: אבל לא לגיטין - היכא דקידושיו היו קידושין גמורין, ותיובתא דרב כהנא:
Rashi on Gittin 71a:11:2.english: But not for bills of divorce - Where his betrothal was a full betrothal, and [this is] a refutation of Rav Kahana:

Rashi on Gittin 71a:12:1.english: In what [case] is this statement said - That they did not follow his [signals or handwriting] in [matters of] bills of divorce:

Rashi on Gittin 71a:12:2.hebrew: בחרש מעיקרו - שאין לו כתב יד של דעת, שלא היתה לו דעת צלולה מימיו. ולקמיה פריך: וכיון דחרש מעיקרו הוא, הרי כנס ברמיזה ולא היו קידושין גמורין; ומוקי לה ביבם:
Rashi on Gittin 71a:12:2.english: In [the case of] a deaf-mute from the outset - for he does not have handwriting of [halakhic] competence, since he never had a clear mind in his life. And later [the Gemara] asks: Since he is a deaf-mute from the outset, he married [her] by gesturing and it was not a full betrothal [so gesturing should suffice for divorce as well]; and [the Gemara] establishes it [as referring] to a yavam [levirate husband]:

Rashi on Gittin 71a:12:3.english: But [one who was] competent - who learned to write with a clear mind:

Rashi on Gittin 71a:12:4.hebrew: הוא כותב - גט, ואחרים חותמין, והיינו כרב כהנא:
Rashi on Gittin 71a:12:4.english: He writes - a bill of divorce, and others sign [it], and this is in accordance with [the opinion of] Rav Kahana:

Rashi on Gittin 71a:13:1.hebrew: כשם שכונס ברמיזה כו' - משנה היא ביבמות, דחרש שנשא אשה אם רצה יוציא:
Rashi on Gittin 71a:13:1.english: Just as he marries [her] by gesturing, etc. - It is a Mishnah in [Tractate] Yevamot, [teaching] that a deaf-mute who married a woman — if he wishes, he may divorce [her]:

Rashi on Gittin 71a:13:2.hebrew: ביבמתו - שקידושיה גמורין וזיקתה גמורה, והוא אין יכול לחלוץ לפי שאינו ב"ועמד ואמר לא חפצתי לקחתה" (דברים כ״ה:ח׳), וכונס ואינו מוציא לעולם, דגט דידיה לא מפקע זיקה דאורייתא:
Rashi on Gittin 71a:13:2.english: With his yevama - whose betrothal [to his brother] is fully valid and whose levirate bond is fully valid, and he cannot perform chalitzah because he is not [included] in "and he shall stand and say, I do not desire to take her" (Deuteronomy 25:8), and [thus] he marries [her] and can never divorce [her], for his bill of divorce does not annul a Torah-level levirate bond:

Rashi on Gittin 71a:17:1.english: His wife as well - let us issue a decree [regarding her] on account of his yevama whose betrothal was complete:

Rashi on Gittin 71a:17:2.english: His yevama with his yevama - [meaning] the wife of his halakhically competent brother with the wife of his deaf-mute brother:

Rashi on Gittin 71a:18:1.english: And do we decree - [with regard to] his deaf-mute brother on account of a halakhically competent [brother]:

Rashi on Gittin 71a:1:1.hebrew: בפירי - שאינם מצוים באותה שעה, כגון צריש"ש בימות הגשמים, ובימות החמה נישפל"ה:
Rashi on Gittin 71a:1:1.english: With produce - [that is, produce] that is not found at that time [of year], such as cherries in the winter, and in the summer, medlars:

Rashi on Gittin 71a:2:1.hebrew: חרש - שהיה פיקח כשכנסה וקדושיו קידושין גמורין, ותנן ביבמות (דף קיב:): "נתחרש הוא או נשתטה, לא יוציא עולמית", לפי שאין כח בגירושי חרשות להפקיע קידושי חכמה; וקאמר רב דאם יכול לדבר מתוך הכתב — דיודע לכתוב על הקלף: "כתבו ותנו גט לאשתי, אתם פלוני ופלוני", ומסר להם — פיקח גמור הוא, וכותבין ונותנין:
Rashi on Gittin 71a:2:1.english: A deaf-mute - [meaning one] who was of sound mind when he married her, and his betrothal is a completely valid betrothal, and we learned in Yevamot (112b): "[If] he became a deaf-mute or became insane, he may never divorce [her]," because a divorce [executed in a state] of deaf-muteness has no power to annul a betrothal [contracted in a state] of sound mind. And Rav says that if he can speak through writing — [meaning] he knows how to write on parchment, "Write and give a bill of divorce to my wife, you, so-and-so and so-and-so," and handed [it] to them — he is completely of sound mind, and they may write and give [it].

Rashi on Gittin 71a:3:1.hebrew: אלם קאמרת שאני אלם - דכיון דשומע הוא, הרי הוא כפיקח לכל דבריו; אבל חרש שאינו שומע ואינו מדבר, אי לאו דיכול לדבר מתוך הכתב, ברמיזה לא מפיק, ואי לאו דאשמעינן רב, לא הוה ידענא:
Rashi on Gittin 71a:3:1.english: A mute, you say? A mute is different - For since he can hear, he is like a [halakhically] competent person in all his matters; however, [regarding] a deaf-mute who neither hears nor speaks, if it were not that he is able to speak through writing, he could not [effect a divorce] through gesturing [alone], and had Rav not taught us [this], I would not have known [it]:

Rashi on Gittin 71a:4:1.hebrew: חרש המדבר ואינו שומע זהו חרש - ולא זהו חרש שדברו בו חכמים בכל מקום והשווהו לשוטה, דזהו כפיקח לכל דבריו כדקתני בהדיא, אבל חרש דרב כהנא (אינו) לא שומע ולא מדבר:
Rashi on Gittin 71a:4:1.english: A deaf person — one who speaks and does not hear, this is a deaf person - And this is not the deaf person of whom the Sages spoke everywhere, equating him to an imbecile [shoteh], for this one is like a competent person in all his matters, as [the baraita] explicitly teaches; rather, the deaf person [of whom] Rav Kahana [spoke] neither hears nor speaks:

Rashi on Gittin 71a:4:2.english: His speech has been taken [ishtakil millulei] - [This is] an acronym [notarikon] for [the word] ilem [mute]:

Rashi on Gittin 71a:5:1.english: If [it is] difficult for me - regarding this [statement] of Rav Kahana:

Rashi on Gittin 71a:5:2.hebrew: פרט לאלם - שאינו חייב קרבן שבועה על שבועת העדות, אם השביעו והרכין בראשו שאינו יודע:
Rashi on Gittin 71a:5:2.english: To exclude a mute - [Meaning] that he is not liable [to bring] an oath offering for an oath of testimony, if [a litigant] adjured him and he nodded his head [to indicate] that he does not know:

Rashi on Gittin 71a:5:3.hebrew: הרי יכול להגיד מתוך הכתב - ואם איתא לדרב כהנא, ליחייב:
Rashi on Gittin 71a:5:3.english: Behold, he is able to utter [testimony] through writing - And if Rav Kahana's [statement] is [correct], let him be liable [to bring an offering]:

Rashi on Gittin 71a:6:1.english: From their mouths - [That is, the verse states:] “By the mouth of two witnesses”:

Rashi on Gittin 71a:6:2.hebrew: ולא מפי כתבם - יעידו בב"ד, דלא דמי לשטר שחתמוהו ביומו, דההוא אורחיה להכי:
Rashi on Gittin 71a:6:2.english: And not from their writing - [that] they should testify in court [in writing], for it is not similar to a document that they signed on its day, since that is its normal manner for this:

Rashi on Gittin 71a:7:1.english: Just as they investigate - [This] refers to [one who] became mute and nodded his head:

Rashi on Gittin 71a:7:2.english: For business transactions and gifts - [i.e.,] to sell his property:

Rashi on Gittin 71a:7:3.english: For testimonies and for inheritances - [the Gemara] goes on to explain all of them:

Rashi on Gittin 71a:7:4.hebrew: קתני מיהא לעדיות - שיעיד עדותו מפי הכתב, והאמרת "מפיהם", וזה נאלם:
Rashi on Gittin 71a:7:4.english: In any event, it teaches: [for] testimonies - [meaning] that he may give his testimony in writing, yet you said "from their mouth" [and not from their writing], whereas this [person] is mute:

Rashi on Gittin 71a:8:1.english: Regarding testimony [concerning] a woman - [Testimony] to permit her to remarry:

Rashi on Gittin 71a:8:2.hebrew: דאקילו בה - בעד אחד, קרוב ושפחה:
Rashi on Gittin 71a:8:2.english: As they were lenient with her - [accepting] a single witness, a relative, and a maidservant:

Rashi on Gittin 71a:9:1.english: And we ask: [It] teaches, "Inheritances" - And it enters your mind [that it refers to] testifying about an inheritance that someone else bequeathed:

Rashi on Gittin 71a:9:2.hebrew: אמר רבי אבהו - מאי "ירושות"? בנו דידיה, אם רצה להשוות את הבכור כאחד מבניו. ולהכי נקט "ירושת בנו הבכור", דאם לא לשנות על משפט הירושה של תורה הוא בא, למה לנו לדבריו? הירושה מאיליה תפול:
Rashi on Gittin 71a:9:2.english: Rabbi Abbahu said - What [is meant by] "inheritances"? [It refers to] his own son — if he wished to make the firstborn equal to [each] one of his [other] sons. And this is why [Rabbi Abbahu] specifically stated "the inheritance of his firstborn son": for if he were not coming to alter the Torah's law of inheritance, why would we need his words? The inheritance would fall [to the heirs] on its own:

Tosafot on Gittin 71a:12:1.hebrew: תנאי היא דתניא אמר רשב"ג כו' - לא בעי לשנויי דרב מיירי בפיקח מעיקרו וברייתא בחרש מעיקרו, כמו שמחלק רשב"ג, משום דקים לן דרשב"ג פליג על הך ברייתא, כדאמר רבי יוחנן בסמוך:
Tosafot on Gittin 71a:12:1.english: It is [a dispute between] tanna'im, as it is taught: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said, etc. - [The Gemara] did not want to answer that Rav is speaking of one who was competent from the outset, and the baraita [is speaking] of one who was a deaf-mute from the outset, as Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel distinguishes — because it is established for us that Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel disagrees with that baraita, as Rabbi Yoḥanan says shortly below:

Tosafot on Gittin 71a:1:1.hebrew: אלא בפירי - אין לפרש ששואלין לו אם רוצה פירי של ימות הגשמים בימות החמה או איפכא, ואומר "הן", כי זה אפשר למצוא בכבושים בדבש או בענין אחר; אלא ששואלין לו אם רוצה שילקטו לו מן האילן:
Tosafot on Gittin 71a:1:1.english: Rather, with produce - One should not explain [this to mean] that they ask him if he wants winter produce in the summer or vice versa, and he says "yes," because this can be found preserved in honey or in another manner; rather, [it means] that they ask him if he wants them to pick [it] for him from the tree:

Tosafot on Gittin 71a:2:1.hebrew: אמר רב יוסף מאי קמ"ל תנינא נשתתק כו' - תימה לר"י: אדרבה, דתיקשי ליה מתני', כיון דאינו מחלק בין אלם לחרש — דלמה לי "יכול לדבר מתוך הכתב", בהרכנה סגי! ואומר ר"י, דהא ודאי דבחרש לא סגי בהרכנה, אע"פ שכותבין לו "נכתוב גט לאשתך" ומרכין בראשו, ובודקין אותו ג"פ לאו והן; אלא דמדמי רב יוסף הרכנה דאלם לכתיבה דחרש: כמו שאלם ע"י הרכנה ניכר שמבין ומתרצה, ועל ידי זה כותבים גט, הוא הדין חרש ששאלוהו בכתב והשיב בכתב, יש הוכחה שהוא מבין בטוב, אע"פ שאם שאלוהו בכתב והרכין בראשו אינו מועיל כלום:
Tosafot on Gittin 71a:2:1.english: Rav Yosef said: What is he teaching us? We learned [in the Mishnah]: [If he] became mute, etc. - This is astonishing to the Ri: on the contrary, the Mishnah should pose a difficulty to him [i.e., to Rav Kahana's statement], since [Rav Yosef] does not distinguish between a mute and a deaf-mute — why do I need "[who] can express [himself] through writing"? Nodding should suffice! And the Ri says that [it is] certainly [true] that for a deaf-mute nodding does not suffice, even though they write to him, "Shall we write a bill of divorce for your wife?" and he nods his head, and they examine him three times [with] "no" and "yes"; rather, Rav Yosef compares the nodding of a mute to the writing of a deaf-mute: just as [for] a mute, through nodding it is evident that he understands and consents, and on this basis they write a bill of divorce, so too [for] a deaf-mute whom they asked in writing and who responded in writing, there is proof that he understands well — even though if they asked him in writing and he nodded his head, it is of no avail at all:

Tosafot on Gittin 71a:5:1.hebrew: אמר רבי זירא אי קשיא כו' - תימה לר"י, דמשמע דפריך לרב כהנא, מדקאמר "והא יכול לדבר מתוך הכתב"; ואמאי לא פריך אמתניתי', דהרי יכול להגיד ע"י הרכנה? ואור"י, דמתניתין לא קשיא ליה, דפשיטא ליה דגבי גט אין צריך הגדה בפה, רק שמתרצה, כמו שצריך גבי עדות דבור; אבל לרב כהנא, דחשיב "יכול לדבר מתוך הכתב" אפי' בחרש, א"כ דבור מעליא הוא, ויש לחושבה הגדה. וי"מ, דאמתניתין לא קשיא ליה, דאיכא למימר דהא דאמר "פרט לאלם שאינו יכול להגיד", היינו אלם שאינו שומע, דהיינו חרש; אבל "אלם" לא משמע הכי:
Tosafot on Gittin 71a:5:1.english: Rabbi Zeira said: If [it is] difficult, etc. - It is astonishing to the Ri that it implies that [Rabbi Zeira] is challenging Rav Kahana, from the fact that he says, "But he can speak through writing"; and why did he not challenge the Mishnah, for [a mute] can utter [his intent] through nodding? And the Ri says that the Mishnah is not difficult for him, because it is obvious to him that regarding a bill of divorce, verbal utterance is not required — only that he consents — as speech is required regarding testimony; however, according to Rav Kahana, who considers "able to speak through writing" [valid] even for a deaf-mute, if so, it is full-fledged speech, and one should consider it an utterance. And some explain that the Mishnah is not difficult for him, because one could say that that which [the baraita] says, "excluding a mute who cannot utter," refers to a mute who does not hear, which is a deaf-mute; however, "mute" does not imply this:

Tosafot on Gittin 71a:5:2.hebrew: והא יכול לדבר מתוך הכתב - דהגדה חשיבה ע"י הכתב כדפרישית, אע"ג דממעט חרש וחרשת מחליצה לפי שאינם ב"אמר" ו"אמרה", אמירה ודאי לא הוי אלא בפה; ועוד, דהתם יליף "וענתה" מ"וענו הלוים", שצריך בלשון הקדש, ומינה נמי שמעינן דהויא בפה כמו בלוים:
Tosafot on Gittin 71a:5:2.english: But he is able to speak through writing - For uttering [testimony] is considered [valid] through writing, as I explained [above]. Even though [the Gemara] excludes a deaf-mute man and a deaf-mute woman from ḥalitzah because they are not included in "he shall say" and "she shall say" — "saying" is certainly only [done] orally. Furthermore, there it derives "and she shall answer" from "and the Levites shall answer" [to teach] that it must be in the Holy Tongue, and from that we also learn that it must be [spoken] orally, just as with the Levites:

Tosafot on Gittin 71a:6:1.hebrew: מפיהם ולא מפי כתבם - בפ' שני דכתובות (דף כ:) הארכתי בה:
Tosafot on Gittin 71a:6:1.english: From their mouths and not from their writing - In the second chapter of Ketubot (20b), I elaborated on it:

Tosafot on Gittin 71a:7:1.hebrew: קתני מיהת עדיות - אמאי דקתני "פרט לאלם שאינו יכול להגיד", פריך. ומיהו לר"י נראה דהאי פירכא נמי הויא לרב, דהא תיובתא דבתר הכי הויא לדידיה. והכי פירושו: בשלמא אי לאו דרב, אע"פ שלענין עדות חשיבה הגדה מה שמרכין בראשו, כדקתני הכא דבודקין אותו לעדות, מ"מ פטר קרא אלם שאינו יכול להגיד, דלענין קרבן שבועה לא חשיבה הגדה אלא הגדה מעליא; אלא לרב, דחשיב דיכול לדבר מתוך הכתב עדות מעליא, כיון דאפילו בחרש מהני אע"ג דהרכנה לא מהניא ביה כלל, וא"כ צריך לומר הא דממעט קרא אלם שאינו יכול להגיד, אע"פ שיכול לדבר מתוך הכתב, משום דרחמנא אמר "מפיהם ולא מפי כתבם"; וא"כ, איך בודקין אותו לעדות? הא בעינן "מפיהם ולא מפי כתבם"! ולמאי דפירשנו "פרט לאלם שאינו יכול להגיד" דהיינו חרש, א"ש: דאי לאו דרב, באלם סגי בהרכנה בכל דבר, אבל חרש לא סגי אפי' יכול לדבר מתוך הכתב, לא לענין גט ולא לענין עדות; אבל לרב, אע"ג דפסול לענין עדות, כשר גבי גט — תקשי ליה, דהא הכא מכשרינן עדות כמו גט:
Tosafot on Gittin 71a:7:1.english: In any event, it teaches: Testimonies - [The Gemara] is raising an objection against that which was taught: "[This comes] to exclude a mute who is unable to utter [his testimony]." However, to Rabbi Yitzchak it appears that this objection is also [directed] against Rav [Kahana], for the refutation that follows is [directed] against him. And this is its explanation: It is understandable were it not for [the view of] Rav [Kahana] — even though with respect to testimony, nodding his head is considered an utterance, as it teaches here that they examine him for testimony, nevertheless the verse exempts a mute who is unable to utter, because with respect to an oath-offering, only a proper [oral] utterance is considered an utterance. However, according to Rav [Kahana], who considers [the fact] that one can speak through writing to be proper testimony — since it is effective even for a deaf-mute, even though nodding is not effective for him at all — if so, one must say that [the reason] the verse excludes a mute who is unable to utter, even though he can speak through writing, is because the Merciful One said, "From their mouths [and not from their writing]." And if so, how can they examine him for testimony? Surely we require "from their mouths and not from their writing"! And according to what we explained [earlier], that "[this comes] to exclude a mute who is unable to utter" refers to a deaf-mute, it works out well: for were it not for [the view of] Rav [Kahana], for a mute [who can hear], nodding suffices in every matter, whereas for a deaf-mute, even if he can speak through writing, it does not suffice, neither with respect to a bill of divorce nor with respect to testimony; whereas according to Rav [Kahana], even though he is disqualified with respect to testimony, he is fit with respect to a bill of divorce — [so] it is difficult for him, since here we validate testimony just like a bill of divorce:

Tosafot on Gittin 71a:9:1.hebrew: והא קתני ירושות - השתא דקסבר ירושות דעלמא, ומשאות ומתנות דעלמא, ולענין עדות קאמר, צ"ל דסלקא דעתיה דפרושי קא מפרש: למשאות ומתנות וירושות — היינו עדות. אי נמי, הוי מצי למימר: ולטעמיך, היינו עדות:
Tosafot on Gittin 71a:9:1.english: But isn’t it taught: Inheritances - Now that [the Gemara] assumes [the baraita refers to] inheritances in general and business transactions and gifts in general, and that it is speaking with regard to testimony, one must say that it occurred to [the Gemara] that [the baraita] is explaining: "[testimony] for business transactions, gifts, and inheritances — that is [what is meant by] 'testimony.'" Alternatively, [the Gemara] could have said: "And according to your reasoning, that is 'testimony'":

Tosafot on Gittin 71a:9:2.hebrew: ירושת בנו הבכור - פרש"י: שהשוה בכור לפשוט. ואין נראה לר"י: אם כן, הוה ליה למימר שריבה לזה ומיעט לזה; אלא אומר רבינו יצחק דהיינו שאומר על בן בין הבנים שהוא בכור, וקא משמע לן דנאמן לכך על ידי הרכנה:
Tosafot on Gittin 71a:9:2.english: The inheritance of his firstborn son - Rashi explained that he equated a firstborn to an ordinary [son]. But this does not seem [correct] to R"I: if so, [the Gemara] should have said that he increased [the portion] for one and decreased [it] for another. Rather, Rabbeinu Yitzchak says that this means he says regarding a son among the sons that he is the firstborn, and [the Gemara] teaches us that he is believed regarding this by means of nodding:
